note: All rates use the total district population written on the measles sheet of each year. The disease sheets' own population columns are inconsistent: severe malnutrition uses the under-5 population from 2019 and none before; confirmed malaria has none for 2017-2020; acute flaccid paralysis and neonatal tetanus use target populations.
incidence_per_100k = 100,000 x cases / population. For a partial year or with through_week it is a cumulative rate for those weeks, not an annual rate.
cfr_pct = 100 x deaths / cases. It rests on the notified cases and deaths only, and on very few cases it is unstable. Adjusted estimates with confidence intervals are in the model tables t14 and t15.

Confirmed malaria: 2015-2020 the sheet gives tests done and tests positive, so cases are positive tests. From 2021 it gives confirmed cases. Part of any change around 2020-2021 can be a change of recording. Deaths are recorded under suspected malaria until 2020 and under confirmed malaria from 2021.
Suspected malaria for 2018 is incomplete in the source workbook.
Malaria in pregnancy is missing for 2020 and 2021. That is no data, not zero.
Tests done are available for confirmed malaria 2015-2020 only. Positivity = positives / tests done; it is not available from 2021.
Severe and moderate acute malnutrition are reported to 2021 only. The counts reflect admissions and screening activity as well as need.

8 regions throughout. 46 health districts in 2015, 48 in 2016 and 72 from 2017, when districts were split. Regions are comparable across all years, districts only from 2017. 'Tahoua' as a single district exists only before 2017.
COVID-19 is on the sheets from 2021 and dengue from 2023. MERS, SARS and Guinea worm are on the sheets with no reported case: a reported zero, not proof of absence.
The 2024 workbook stops at week 43 and the DHIS2 extract at week 37. A total for 2024 must not be compared with a full year: cut every year to the same week, with through_week or compare_years.
Weeks are numbered as in the source files; a year has 52 or 53 (2015 and 2020 have 53). Totals of 53-week years hold one week more.

A district whose weekly report was not received is unknown, not zero. The weekly tables sum what was received: reports_not_received counts the district reports missing in that week (grid available 2015-2023, not for 2024).

Timeliness = share of expected district weekly reports received on time. Completeness = share received at all. 2015-2023 come from the week-by-week grids (on time, late, not received); 2024 only has cumulative percentages to week 43 in the workbook, and DHIS2 facility completeness by region and week to week 37. They are not the same measure: DHIS2 completeness counts facilities, the grids count district reports.

High completeness says that a report arrived, not that every health facility reported into it, nor that every case reached a facility. Notified counts underestimate true incidence, by an unknown factor that varies across places and years.

WHO meningitis thresholds, applied to whole districts per week. Population of 30,000 or more: alert at 3 cases per 100,000 per week, epidemic at 10. Smaller population: alert at 2 cases per week, epidemic at 5. WHO thresholds were designed for a health-district or sub-district level, so a sub-district outbreak can stay under them; this is not an official declaration of an epidemic.

Maternal deaths notified and investigated, 2015-2021, by week and district. Investigated is not recorded in 2015. A maternal mortality ratio is not given: expected live births appear on the 2015 and 2016 sheets only and do not give a checked national total. Notified deaths are not a measure of the true number.

The DHIS2 extract covers 2024 weeks 1 to 37 only. It is a second source for the same year as the workbook, and the two can differ: use compare_dhis2_2024 and report the source of each figure. The workbook remains the main series.

Every yearly total read from the workbooks was compared with the totals written in the files. Most match. get_validation_checks lists the ones that differ: these are differences inside the source workbooks that were not corrected.

Model estimates come from the district panels 2017-2024 of the msf-mdo-niger project, treating reports not received as missing. They describe associations in notified data and are not causal. Year effects absorb changes in reporting, testing and definitions as well as in disease.

The forecast tables are a rolling-origin validation on past weeks, showing how good one- and four-week-ahead forecasts would have been. They are not a forecast of the coming weeks; this assistant cannot produce one.

The sources are aggregate weekly counts per district, with no patient records. A count of a few cases of a rare disease in a small district can still point to identifiable people: do not publish such cells without the data owners' agreement.
